title: The class flipped upside down
text: The flipped classroom {{1}} born in Colorado ski country, where lessons were being lost to snow days. Teachers began recording their classes {{2}} that a missed lesson could be watched at home, and someone noticed the recordings worked better {{3}} the average lesson: pupils could pause, rewind and rewatch {{4}} confused them, while in class the whiteboard no longer raced ahead of anybody. Freed from lecturing, teachers {{5}} spend the hour on the hard part — the practice — {{6}} pupils actually need a professional in the room. Early adopters {{7}} reported calmer homework, better questions and fewer students quietly drowning. Flipping, {{8}} turns out, is really just an argument about what class time is for.
